messages:
ajay: heads-up — I'm going to start a canary rollout for the edge client v2 feature gating that uses request headers. planning to enable for 2% of traffic first. comments on header format and safety checks?

maria: +1 to canary. prefer explicit header name rather than overloaded cookie. also need a strong server-side fallback if header missing or malformed. :thumbsup:

natalie: suggest format: `X-Redwood-Client-Feature: client_v2=true;canary=hash( user_id )%<N>`

ajay: example I had in mind:
```
X-Redwood-Feature: client=v2;canary=2
```
server should treat `canary` as percent threshold, not a whitelist. if header absent we use version in SDK, and if SDK < 2.0 we MUST not enable features that require new wire format.

samir: for deterministic canary by user id we do something like: `hash(user_id) % 100 < 2` (2%). we already use that in rollout service. we should centralize the logic server-side so clients only send the header, not compute hashes locally.

maria: agree centralize. also add a server-side kill switch key (env var + rollout API) so we can immediately disable for all traffic.

ajay: QA checklist proposal:
- create canary config in rollout service for header-based gating (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- add validation: header schema, allowed keys, max length
- server fallback: if header present but client version < 2.0 -> log + ignore gating (no crash)
- telemetry: emit `feature_flag.evaluated` with fields `{flag: client_v2, decision: on|off, reason: header|sdk|fallback}`
- create alert: error_rate_or_latency_delta > 3x baseline after canary step

natalie: addendum — record `client_sdk_version` in the telemetry event so we can track backcompat issues.

dev-rel-bot: note: SDK PR #412 will include header serialization and a runtime feature to opt-in for local computation. we recommend disabling local canary computation for now (server side wins). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 :eyes:

release-bot: rolling canary requires these env flags: `FEATURE_HEADER_GATING=true`, `FEATURE_HEADER_KILLSWITCH=off`, `CANARY_PERCENT=2`. I'll create the rollout draft and tag owners.

ajay: guardrails we should enforce:
- validate header length and characters (reject and metrics if invalid)
- rate-limit header-based routes per client-id to avoid misuse
- require opt-in feature flag in account for enterprise tenants (no header override)
- automatically revert if `5xx_rate` increases by >1% or p50 latency increases by >50ms

maria: also add a unit test for the header parser and an e2e that asserts old clients continue to get legacy responses.

samir: for canary audience exceptions (internal QA) we should allow a `user_allowlist` param in rollout service so QA accounts can be forced on regardless of percent. log those hits with `canary_reason=allowlist`.

ajay: roll steps and owners:
- natalie: rollout config + telemetry events schema (PR by EOD)
- maria: API validation + backward compatibility tests (PR by tomorrow)
- dev-rel-bot: SDK change + release notes (coordinate with QA)
- samir: rollout service wiring + allowlist (small PR)
- release-bot: create canary plan and monitor thresholds

natalie: reviewer ping: @maria @samir — will need quick review once I open PR.

maria: I'll review later today. may ask to change metric names to `feature.client_v2.*` for consistency.

ajay: thanks — final: please react with :thumbsup: when you've wired your PRs. I'll wait for all thumbs then flip the `CANARY_PERCENT` to 2% and watch dashboards.

samir: :thumbsup: will add allowlist and the deterministic check.

dev-rel-bot: added draft changelog entry: "Edge client v2 header gating (canary) — SDK opt-in disabled by default"

release-bot: created canary ticket in Jira: RD-2345, linked PRs in ticket. will post status here on each step.
